title: 12 · From editor node to runtime bytes

chapters.title: b2
chapters.text: The full toolchain, end to end. This is the chapter to re-read when a graph "doesn't do anything", because the answer is always which stage did it die at.

chapters.title: b4
chapters.text: Stage by stage, with the failure signature

chapters.title: b6
chapters.text: Doing this in code rather than by hand in the graph window is the difference between a reproducible project and an artifact nobody dares regenerate. Nerve's own sample builds its graphs this way; so does ours (Assets/Editor/Client Graph Setup.cs).

chapters.title: b7
chapters.text: Failure signature: Try Set Value returns false then you used the wrong option name. Our helper throws and prints every available option, which turns a 20-minute hunt into a one-line message.

chapters.title: b9
chapters.text: [Use With Graph(typeof(Client Nerve Graph))] on a node is the gate. Put a Client Go In Game Node in a.snerve and the toolkit will not offer it.

chapters.title: b10
chapters.text: Failure signature: graph asset imports but Asset Database.Load Asset At Path<Nerve Graph Auth> returns null then the importer did not run, usually a stale Library/.

chapters.title: b12
chapters.text: Runs on every graph change and at bake. Our setup script re-checks explicitly and throws, so a broken graph fails at build time rather than as a silent no-op at runtime.

chapters.title: b14
chapters.text: Note file ID: 9196009390298549883, the Nerve Graph Auth is a sub-asset inside the.cnerve file, not the file itself. Both the guid and the file ID must be right.

chapters.title: b15
chapters.text: Failure signature: 'X' is missing a Nerve graph. at bake.

chapters.title: b17
chapters.text: baker.Depends On is what makes editing the graph re-bake the subscene. Omit it and you edit a graph, see no change, and lose an hour.

chapters.title: b18
chapters.text: Failure signature: graph edits have no runtime effect then missing Depends On, or the subscene did not re-import.

chapters.title: b20
chapters.text: The entity now carries Nerve State Machine { Graph, State Id } and a Dynamic Buffer<Grove State>. The executor's query is With All RW<Grove State>().With All RW<Nerve State Machine>(), if either is missing, the system finds nothing and does nothing, quietly.

chapters.title: b22
chapters.text: When a graph does nothing, walk down this list; the first no is your bug.

chapters.title: b23
chapters.text: We used exactly this ladder to land the client graph, and steps 5, 7 are where the two non-obvious hops live.

chapters.title: b25
chapters.text: Part II done. You can now read every package in the stack. Time for the wire.
